title: ISE Group-Based Policy (GBP / Microsegmentation) Effective-Policy Drift
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'ISE Group-Based Policy (GBP / Microsegmentation) Effective-Policy Drift' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_ise_group_based_policy_gbp_microsegmentation_eff` (UC-17.1.76), SOC dashboard panel "Network — ISE Group-Based Policy (GBP / Microsegmentation) Effective-Policy Drift", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.assurance_rationale: SOX ITGC change management — segmentation policy changes.
CM-3 configuration change control — segmentation matrix.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=target_index` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `entity` satisfies detection threshold for UC-17.1.76 ('ISE Group-Based Policy (GBP / Microsegmentation) Effective-Policy Drift'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `target_index` / `target_sourcetype` events where `entity` stays below detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.76.

dataSources: ISE configuration data via OpenAPI (`/ers/config/sgmatrix`, `/ers/config/sgt`) — periodic export of the SGT-to-SGT (source-to-destination) policy matrix into a Splunk lookup `ise_sgt_matrix.csv`. ISE syslog *Authorization* — codes `5402`, `5403` for dynamic SGT-policy compilation events. Compare current matrix against baseline `ise_sgt_matrix_baseline.csv`. Collected via Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services`. — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)
spl:
| inputlookup ise_sgt_matrix.csv 
| join type=outer source_sgt destination_sgt [| inputlookup ise_sgt_matrix_baseline.csv | rename action as baseline_action]
| eval drift=if(action!=baseline_action, "DRIFTED", "ok")
| where drift=="DRIFTED"
description: Detects unauthorised changes to the SGT-to-SGT effective policy matrix. Compares each cell of the current matrix against the approved baseline and flags any drift.
value: Detects unauthorised changes to the SGT-to-SGT effective policy matrix. Timely UC-17.1.76 alerting on 'ISE Group-Based Policy (GBP / Microsegmentation) Effective-Policy Drift' reduces unauthorized access, segmentation drift, and NAC policy failures before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Daily. Requires a curated baseline CSV checked into version control.
visualization: Drift cells over time; current matrix vs. baseline visualization.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `target_index`** — Planned work for 'ISE Group-Based Policy (GBP / Microsegmentation) Effective-Policy Drift' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `host` remains in-scope for UC-17.1.76. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `configured_sourcetype`** — Scheduled automation elevates `drift` without crossing configured threshold. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `target_index` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `configured_sourcetype`** — First 48h baseline for `host` is unstable; join `ise_sgt_matrix.csv` prior to threshold.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
mitreAttack: N/A (policy hygiene — measures Group-Based Policy hit counts, no adversary technique)
detailedImplementation:
Standard pattern.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services`. — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`drift`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: The microsegmentation matrix is a big spreadsheet of which device groups can talk to which. We check it daily against the approved version and flag any cell that has changed.
